chunks: What Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Abī Najrān, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, who said:
Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said:

Sajdah is upon seven bones: the forehead, the two hands, the two knees, and the two big toes of the feet. And press your nose down in humility. As for the obligation, it is these seven; and as for pressing the nose down, it is a sunnah from the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم.

key_terms.الْإِرْغَامُ: pressing the nose onto the ground in sajdah
key_terms.الْجَبْهَةِ: the forehead, one of the obligatory points of prostration
key_terms.سَبْعَةِ أَعْظُمٍ: the seven bodily bones or limbs upon which sajdah is performed
key_terms.سُنَّةٌ: a recommended prophetic practice, not obligatory

ai.seo_question: What are the obligatory limbs for sajdah in salat (prayer), and is placing the nose required?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the required bodily points for sajdah in salat (prayer), specifying seven limbs upon which prostration is performed. It distinguishes between what is obligatory in sajdah and what is sunnah (prophetic tradition), namely pressing the nose upon the ground.
